clue.text: A limit to Rome's influence in Britain?

definitions.text: A limit to Rome's influence in Britain?

parts.words: A limit to Rome's influence in Britain?
parts.note: read as history, the clue describes the stone barrier across northern England that marked the edge of Roman rule

explanation.surface: A question about how far Roman power reached in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'limit' is literal: the emperor's fortified barrier across northern England was the frontier of Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortification built under an emperor across northern England was the northern frontier of the Roman province.

clue.text: Collision getting female into trouble, or the reverse!

indicators.note: the word into first suggests putting the female inside the trouble
this phrase flips the order, so the trouble goes inside the female instead

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A crash that lands a woman in trouble, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' alone would put HEN inside ADO; 'or the reverse' tells you to put ADO inside HEN instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision in which two vehicles meet front to front is described with this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Glaring extortion by God in connivance with the library

indicators.note: words acting in connivance plot together, so the letters of the two phrases are scheming into a new order

explanation.surface: An outrageous swindle in which God secretly conspires with the library.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BY GOD and THE LIBRARY together are rearranged to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blatant overcharging is called this idiom, as if the robbery happened openly in broad sunlight.

clue.text: Ethereal juice featured in Gothic horror

indicators.note: something featured in a piece is contained within it, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A ghostly fluid that turns up in a Gothic horror story.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the ethereal fluid that flows in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

clue.text: 12 traps badger with 9 sides

indicators.note: the first piece traps the second, holding it inside itself

parts.note: twelve o'clock, midday, is noon
to badger is to nag

explanation.surface: Twelve snares catch a badger, in a figure with nine sides.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to another clue but here is simply twelve o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygon having nine edges and nine angles carries this geometric name.

clue.text: Writer in car with first photographer!

indicators.note: the setter goes in the car, inside its letters

parts.note: taken as written
in crosswords the writer is the setter, me
A is the first letter, or a first-class grade

explanation.surface: An author sits in a car alongside the first photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: The device does the actual photographing, so the clue playfully calls the apparatus a photographer.

clue.text: A lot of parasites stay in her hair

parts.note: lice are parasites living in hair
a band is a group or lot of people

explanation.surface: A crowd of parasites makes its home in her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of parasites' reads as A BAND of LICE; the charade puts LICE before BAND. A stay is a support, and this hairband holds hair back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair accessory, a curved horseshoe band named after the girl in Tenniel's illustrations, holds a woman's hair in place.

clue.text: Of more than ground-breaking importance?

parts.note: taken literally, something more than ground-breaking would smash the whole planet to pieces

explanation.surface: Asking about something even more significant than a breakthrough.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground-breaking means innovative; the literal step up from breaking the ground is shattering the entire globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous enough to seem to shatter the planet is described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Opening copier with true reproduction

parts.note: an aper is one who apes, a copier

indicators.note: a reproduction remakes the original, so these letters are refashioned in another order

explanation.surface: Opening a photocopier that makes faithful reproductions.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE rearranged gives TURE, which follows APER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or gap, as in a camera lens, is an opening.

clue.text: Gay Ninth movement offers whatever

indicators.note: movement of letters means they are shifted into a new order, here those of the two words before

explanation.surface: A cheerful movement of a ninth symphony offers all sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical, with the Ninth a symphony; it signals that GAY and NINTH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: As a pronoun, any thing at all, no matter what, is the same as whatever.

clue.text: Stab king in arm?

indicators.note: the king goes in the arm, inside its letters

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, a gun, which is a piece in slang
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Stabbing a king in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' suggests a limb but means a firearm, a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab is to puncture or pierce through with a pointed blade.

clue.text: See 1across
When cycling, cider girl finds twig

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from the front of the name to its back

parts.note: Rosie is the girl of Laurie Lee's memoir Cider with Rosie

explanation.surface: Out on a bike ride, a girl with cider comes across a twig.
explanation.walkthrough: Cider with Rosie is a much-loved English memoir of a Cotswold childhood; its title girl is ROSIE. Cycling moves her R to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow shoot, used for basket-weaving, is a slender twig.

clue.text: What's fired pot Reg has thrown

indicators.note: thrown suggests pottery on a wheel, and here signals the letters being tossed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Reg has thrown a pot on the wheel, ready to be fired in the kiln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' and 'thrown' play on pottery: POT, REG and HAS are rearranged, and what's fired is a cannon load.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of small iron balls once loaded into a cannon is what gets fired.

clue.text: Scorer at the crease after cut

indicators.note: the batting piece comes after the cutting piece

parts.note: to chop is to cut
a batsman at the crease is in, batting, in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman scores runs after a cutting stroke at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks like cricket but is a composer, who writes scores; the crease is where a cricket batsman stands, being 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish composer wrote piano scores, so he is a scorer.

clue.text: Almost pay cost of accommodation, and get on line

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: rent is what you pay for accommodation
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: Barely managing the rent, and trying to get on the phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line is one's lineage or descent, the family one comes from.

clue.text: Mad king binds the skin

indicators.note: the king binds the word the, holding it inside his name

parts.note: Shakespeare's King Lear goes mad

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch ties up the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned animal hide, used for shoes and bags, is skin.

clue.text: Arab quarrelling with Lord Barker

indicators.note: words quarrelling are at odds and scrambled together into a new order

explanation.surface: An Arab argues with a peer named Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like a surname but means a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever breed of dog, and dogs bark.

clue.text: Men of Lancaster, for example

parts.note: a Lancaster was a Second World War RAF bomber, and the men aboard it flew it as a team

explanation.surface: Asking about the men of the Lancashire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancaster' suggests the northern English city, but it is the RAF's wartime heavy bomber, flown by a crew of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The flying team of any plane, such as a bomber, are its crew members.

clue.text: Driver in forest

definitions.meaning: in golf, the driver is a club with a large head, traditionally made of timber
a forest or copse is a stretch of trees

explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a golf club of this traditional kind, and a small forest is called this too.

clue.text: Do turns in gallery until now

indicators.note: the turned word goes in the gallery, inside its name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: turns means the little word do is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A party goes round and round in the art gallery right up to now.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous group of British art galleries, so TATE stands for gallery; OD goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to the present moment is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: What might, given time, do leap explosively?

definitions.text: What might, given time, do leap explosively?

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters of the two words before are scattered

explanation.surface: What creature might, if you wait long enough, leap with a burst of energy?
explanation.walkthrough: T followed by DO LEAP rearranged; the whole clue also describes the creature that in time becomes a frog and leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva that grows into a frog will, given time, jump about.

clue.text: One carrying weight this minute… (2,4) …so to be seen for a period?

indicators.note: the first piece carries the second inside itself

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone lugging a weight right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The text after the ellipsis belongs to the next clue, 23 down, which continues this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately, right now, is the sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Old boy in hospital gets cross about robber

indicators.note: the cross goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church
OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil in hospital gets angry about a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective, angry, but is a noun, ROOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest robbed the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: Visible hole to left of green

indicators.note: in an across answer the first piece is written to the left of the second

parts.note: O is hole-shaped
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golf hole lies to the left of the green, in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole' and 'green' suggest golf; vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open and unconcealed is visible.

clue.text: …so to be seen for a period?

annotationWithheld.why: …so to be seen for a period? (5): OBESE is hidden in 'to be seen', the same words that would signal the hiding, and the definition 'One carrying weight' sits in 21-down's clue
annotationWithheld.clue: …so to be seen for a period?

clue.text: River bird providing sounds

parts.note: the Dee is a British river
a jay is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird by a river is singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey is someone whose job is supplying the music at a club or on air.

clue.text: Bah! I'm Neo, wonderfully off-beat

indicators.note: wonderfully suggests the letters are worked into a marvellous new arrangement

explanation.surface: The setter Neo dismisses himself as gloriously unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: Neo is the setter, putting his own name into the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An unconventional, artistic lifestyle is called this, so it is off-beat.

clue.text: Poet finding hymn short-rights?

annotationWithheld.why: Poet finding hymn short-rights? (6): HYM (hymn short) leaves R, E, R, which 'rights' as printed cannot give; probably an OCR misreading and no source gives the original

clue.text: In dispute with bird, this one might be disagreeable!

definitions.text: In dispute with bird, this one might be disagreeable!

indicators.note: in dispute means jumbled together, so the answer's letters mixed with those of bird form the last word

explanation.surface: A bird of prey squabbling with another bird turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus BIRD, rearranged, gives DISAGREEABLE: the bird 'in dispute' with this one makes the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A large coastal raptor, a bird of prey, is the one meant here.
